label: late original phase / delimiter, after several l/3/2/h/p/g/i tokens
explanation: Fires in the second half of the original phase (t>=4, peaking at t=5-7) and on the <DEL> step (rate 16%, 22% of mass), sometimes spilling onto the first copy step or two. It is silent at t=0-1 and nearly silent through the copy phase (3% of mass). Within that window it acts like an evidence accumulator over a set of input tokens: l (strongest), 3, 2, h, p, g, i. Activation is higher when these appear at the current step or one to two steps earlier, and the top examples contain several of them, often two l tokens. It is also more frequent in longer sequences and in sequences with more digits. Requiring at least two such tokens so far captures about 83% of activation mass, but precision is only about 0.3: many steps late in the sequence with these tokens stay below threshold, so the trigger set and the counting rule are only approximate.
